label: sec:path-integrals-intro
html:
This chapter initiates Part II by passing from Step 1 of the five-step arc (the rigid braided monoidal category (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) of Part I) to Step 2: the algebraic mechanics of the braid group B_n and its Iwahori–Hecke quotient H_n(q). In a quantum observable universe whose base and fibres have finite cohomological rank, continuum path integrals \int \mathcal{D}\phi are replaced by finite algebraic traces over braid operators acting on tensor powers A^{\otimes n} of the Frobenius–Hopf object. Because the trace is evaluated over a finite-dimensional algebra over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}], ultraviolet divergences do not arise.

The braiding isomorphism c_{A,A} \colon A \otimes A \xrightarrow{\sim} A \otimes A induced by the universal R-matrix of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) satisfies the Yang–Baxter equation and generates a representation of Artin's braid group B_n. Factoring through the quadratic Hecke relation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 yields the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(q), equipped with the Kazhdan–Lusztig bar involution and the Jones–Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the three-row Young weight y_{(1^3)} vanishes identically, forcing the three-strand antisymmetric channel to be evaluated via the Geer–Patureau-Mirand–Turaev modified trace.
